`lineCount` is derived from `r.end.line - r.start.line`, but LSP ranges are end-exclusive at the *character* level. When `r.end.character > 0`, the `end.line` is still part of the range, so the current calculation undercounts by 1 line (e.g. start line 10, end line 12, end.character 5 should include 3 lines, not 2). Consider incorporating `end.character` when converting the LSP range to a line count for `offset`/`limit`.

LSP ranges are end-exclusive by spec: the range [1,4) covers 0-based lines 1-3 (1-based 2-4), and a non-zero end.character on the exclusive end line does not add an extra line. \lineCount = end.line - start.line\ is therefore the correct line span; the character offset only matters if the end line were inclusive, which it isn't for document symbols.

`mergeStringList` currently keeps non-string entries from the previous bucket (`if (typeof item !== "string") return true`). This can persist invalid values into `recentlyClosed`/`hiddenClosed`/`archivedClosed`, and later callers assume strings and pass values to `pathKey(...)`, which will throw on non-strings.

Batch "Forget" builds the list of projects to remove from `filtered()`, so any selected projects that are currently filtered out (e.g. after changing query/filter while in selection mode) will not be forgotten even though they remain counted as selected.

The name tie-breaker comparator never returns 0 for equal pathKeys. If two entries normalize to the same pathKey (or are identical), `Array.prototype.sort` may produce unstable results and can violate the comparator contract, leading to inconsistent ordering across runtimes.

Selection state is only reset when filter/query change, but it can also become stale when the underlying closed list changes (e.g., items removed/reopened, or new history arrives). This can leave `ui.selected` containing worktrees that no longer exist in the current list, and those rows can become unexpectedly selected if they reappear later. Consider also resetting selection when `props.items` changes (or pruning `ui.selected` against the current `filtered()` list).

The workflow sets an explicit `permissions:` block but doesn’t grant `contents: read`, which `actions/checkout` needs to fetch the repository. With explicit permissions, omitted scopes default to `none`, so checkout can fail.
Other workflows in this repo pin `actions/checkout` to a full commit SHA (supply-chain hardening). This new workflow uses the floating `@v4` tag, which is inconsistent and less deterministic.

Optional: this new non-200 status notice means `output` is no longer purely the requested `format` (notably for `format: "html"`), but the opening description still says it "Returns the content in the specified format". Clarifying that the notice is plain text and may precede the body would help avoid callers assuming strict HTML/markdown/text when status != 200.

Good catch - clarified in 1b11fad. The usage note now says a plain-text "[HTTP <status> ...]" line precedes the body regardless of the requested format, and the opening description mentions it too, so `format: "html"` callers are not left assuming the output is strictly markup.

`reload()` rebuilds the strategy registry by replaying the active `ctx.worktree.transform(...)` callbacks against fresh defaults. That recomputes the available strategies, selected default, and configured parent directory.

It is the existing `State.reload()` behavior, moved with the registration state. The config adapter also calls it when its loaded config entries change, so those transforms see the new values.

The distinction is:

```ts
ctx.worktree.reload()               // replay registration/config transforms
ctx.worktree.refresh({ projectID }) // discover worktrees and update saved inventory
```

`reload()` does not rerun plugin setup or discover worktrees. It remains a plugin-only method; it is not an additional HTTP/SDK worktree endpoint.

Implementation: [`State.reload`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b8a7f03ced/packages/core/src/state.ts#L192-L245) and the [config adapter](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b8a7f03ced/packages/core/src/config/plugin/worktree.ts#L19-L21).

This file only scheduled a background `refresh()` whenever a location booted. The discovery/reconciliation implementation itself is still in [`Worktree.refresh`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b8a7f03ced/packages/core/src/worktree.ts#L291).

I removed the location-boot trigger and replaced it with explicit project-based calls at the UI demand points:

- [App inventory loader](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b8a7f03ced/packages/app/src/workspaces/inventory.ts#L49): first demand for a project starts discovery; `worktree.updated` causes a saved-inventory re-read.
- [TUI worktree picker](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b8a7f03ced/packages/tui/src/component/dialog-workspaces.tsx#L95): opening it or pressing refresh runs discovery.
- The TUI Open dialog and app session-workspace menu also explicitly refresh when opened for a project.

The reason was to stop every location boot from independently discovering the same shared project. The behavior change is that simply loading a location no longer discovers external worktrees. Non-UI callers use `worktree.refresh({ projectID })` explicitly; `list` stays a database read.

Agreed. The project-bound wrapper is unnecessary; this should remain a single `ops` object with explicit project arguments:

```ts
ops.list(projectID)
ops.find(projectID, directory)
ops.create(projectID, input, tx?)
ops.remove(projectID, directory, tx?)
```

I introduced `inventory(projectID)` just to capture the ID for the SQL predicates. Passing it directly is simpler, preserves the existing naming, and avoids recreating the helper object and functions for each binding.

Calling **`ctx.worktree.create(...)` from plugin setup in the canonical checkout currently works** because this PR has an explicit fast path:

```ts
// PluginHost passes its existing registry:
worktrees.create(input, currentWorktreeStrategies)

// load() returns before awaiting activation:
if (current?.directory === directory) return current.get()
```

That uses registrations made so far; later plugins have not necessarily registered yet. There is a [server test for this setup call](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b8a7f03ced/packages/server/test/worktree.test.ts#L305).

Your concern applies when that fast path is bypassed—for example, calling the ordinary SDK/HTTP endpoint from setup—or when setup calls form a cycle between projects. Those can still wait on their own activation.

I checked the plugin loader, readiness service, and plugin bridge, and did not find a reusable guard that turns this into a friendly error. Currently [`awaitActivation` is just `ready.await`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b8a7f03ced/packages/core/src/plugin.ts#L250-L254); the latch is held closed during activation. The existing approach here is avoiding the same-runtime wait, rather than detecting and rejecting it.

A friendly-error guard would need to identify a call originating from the activation it is about to await. Checking only whether plugins are loading would also reject normal API callers that should legitimately wait.

Updated in b051e91390: remove now loads the canonical runtime and awaits plugin activation before resolving the worktree’s recorded strategy. It still ignores the currently selected default and returns `StrategyUnavailableError` when the recorded owner did not register. I also updated the HTTP description/docs and changed the server coverage to evict the canonical runtime first, then verify removal reloads the custom strategy.

Implemented in 519de27b5d. The project-bound `inventory(projectID)` wrapper is gone; this is a single `ops` object again, with explicit arguments: `ops.list(projectID)`, `ops.find(projectID, directory)`, `ops.create(projectID, input, tx?)`, and `ops.remove(projectID, directory, tx?)`. Core typecheck and all 35 worktree tests pass.

🟠 **Major** — Design sign-off needed: this resumes live publication of `session.message.content.updated`, which #48043 deliberately retired ("remove message content mutation API"), and which is documented as replay-only (`packages/schema/src/session-event.ts:135`) and excluded from the public manifest. It is mechanically sound — the projector still folds it, the event never reaches SSE clients (`event-feed.ts:49` filters on `isOpenCodeEvent`), and `UsageRecorded` sets a precedent for internal durable events the runner publishes live — but it re-opens the content-mutation path that removal closed, minus the guards the old public API enforced (message completed, no unfinished tools, session idle). Before merge, get an explicit ack from the maintainer who owns #48043 that this internal revival is the intended direction; if it lands, the `// Replay-only` comment should be updated so the file does not misdocument itself. This is not a code defect — it is a merge decision that belongs to the maintainers, flagged so it is made consciously.

🟠 **Major** — This gates the missing-name check on first terminal arrival, but the `finished` computation just below (`mistral-chat.ts:692-695`) still lacks the matching `state.finishReason === undefined` guard that `openai-chat.ts:1083-1087` has — and this PR is what makes that path reachable. Before it, every post-finish frame returned early or failed, so per-frame `finishAll` could only ever run on the first terminal chunk; now a trailing chunk that repeats the terminal `finish_reason` *and* carries content (or a tool delta) skips the early return at line 663, reaches `finished`, and finalizes every accumulated late tool call on the spot with only the arguments received so far.

Trace for:

```
delta({}, "stop")
delta({tool_calls:[{index:0,id:"Ab12Cd34E",function:{name:"lookup",arguments:'{"city":'}}]})
delta({content:"!"}, "stop")   // repeated terminal + late content
delta({tool_calls:[{index:0,function:{arguments:'"Paris"}'}}]})
```

Frame 3 finalizes the call with `{"city":` (partial-parse fallback), clears `tools`, and frame 4's continuation lands in `pendingTools` where `finishEvents` never looks — the response dispatches `lookup` with empty input, silently. That is the same failure class holny found in the previous revision for OpenAI Chat; here it needs a provider that keeps `finish_reason` populated on its trailing chunk, which is one of the shapes this PR exists to absorb.

Adding the first-terminal gate defers finalization to `finishEvents`, where the arguments are complete:

```ts
  const finished =
    state.finishReason === undefined &&
    !incomplete &&
    Object.keys(withTools.tools).length > 0
      ? yield* ToolStream.finishAll(ADAPTER, withTools.tools)
      : undefined
```

(Plain code block rather than a GitHub suggestion because those lines sit just outside the diff hunk.) A test mirroring the OpenAI split-args case with a repeated `finish_reason` would pin it.

🟡 **Minor** — Two behaviors this PR introduces are still unasserted:

1. **Malformed late tool deltas are dropped, not fatal** (your point 3). Nothing here fails today if that regresses into an `InvalidProviderOutput`: a fixture like `deltaChunk({ tool_calls: [{ index: 1, function: { arguments: "{}" } }] })` after the terminal chunk should finish the stream with `toolCalls: []` and no error.
2. **Late reasoning is absorbed** — the motivating SenseNova shape. A trailing `deltaChunk({ reasoning_content: "..." })` should surface in `response.reasoning`; only late text is covered today.

Both are single-fixture additions to this suite.

🟡 **Minor** — The late-content assertion now lives inside "ignores non-text output parts and rejects invalid stream endings", making that test responsible for three unrelated behaviors and its failures ambiguous. Splitting it into its own `it.effect("absorbs content after a terminal chunk", ...)` — the name the OpenAI-compatible suite already uses — keeps the two suites symmetrical.

Confirmed the Mistral issue with a repeated terminal finish and split tool arguments. Without the guard, partial JSON became `{}` and the continuation was dropped.

Fixed in `a012e57d00` by restricting per-frame Mistral finalization to the first terminal arrival. Added regression coverage for this case, malformed late tools, late reasoning, and isolated Mistral late-content handling.

`Math.min` only enforces the upper bound; a plugin config hook can mutate the already-loaded config to `maxDelayMs: -1` or `NaN` (the hook runs without schema revalidation). In those cases `cap()` returns a negative or `NaN` delay, despite the guarantee in its comment, and `next`/`Duration.millis` receive an invalid value. Normalize this limit to a finite non-negative number before storing it.

This issue also appears on line 109 of the same file.

Right, and it's the argument I'd made in the comment just above it: the plugin hook skips revalidation, so an upper bound alone wasn't enough. Fixed in `resolve()` rather than for `maxDelayMs` alone, since every field has the same exposure. Each one now falls back to its default unless it passes the same rule as the schema. That also catches `maxRetries: NaN`, which the old check read as unlimited. Tests for both.

On regenerating the SDK and `openapi.json`: `generate.yml` does that on every push to `dev`, so I've left the generated files alone.

The trigger matcher is intended to allow alphanumerics, `-`, and `_`, but the hyphen between `9` and `_` creates the `9-_` character range. Tokens such as `$foo@bar` therefore match and open the skills popover unexpectedly. Move the hyphen to the end of the class or escape it.

This issue also appears on line 1016 of the same file.

The input matcher is cursor-aware, so the popover can be active for `$re` when more text follows the cursor. But this selection check requires the token to be at the end of the full draft; it then falls through to the normal command handlers, which replace/clear the entire prompt instead of preserving the suffix. Use the editor cursor/range when replacing the trigger.

This reconstructs the draft with only one text part and image parts. If the user has an existing `@` file/agent mention, selecting a `$` suggestion silently removes that mention and its attachment metadata. Replace only the `$...` text range while retaining the other prompt parts.

The `$` popover is opened using the full slash-command list, which contains built-ins and ordinary custom/MCP commands as well as skills. As a result, `$re` can offer and select a non-skill `/review` command, so this is not a skill-only trigger. Preserve the command source and filter this path to skill-backed entries (as the TUI does).

The V2 `$` branch also routes into the generic command popover. The commands supplied by the app include every slash option and server command, so selecting `$name` can invoke or insert an ordinary command instead of a skill. The V2 command list needs a skill-only source/filter for this trigger.

This issue also appears on line 105 of the same file.

`inputChanged` can open this popover when the cursor is before trailing text, because the matcher is cursor-aware. On selection, however, `current` is the full draft and this dollar-specific branch only matches when the token is at the end; otherwise `replaceTrigger(current, "/", ...)` can return only the replacement (or target an unrelated slash), discarding the rest of the draft. Replace the trigger using the persisted cursor/range and preserve the suffix.
Fixed — hyphen moved to the end of the class (`[a-zA-Z0-9_-]`) in all four matchers, and bare `$` is now supported via an optional group that still rejects `$HOME`/``/currency.
Fixed — skill selection now replaces only the `` range at the editor cursor (setRangeEdge start/end) instead of matching the full draft, so trailing text is preserved.
Fixed — selection does a DOM-range replacement of the `` and re-parses via handleInput, so existing @ file/agent pills and attachments are retained. The draft-reconstruction path is removed.

Fixed - $ popover now uses a dedicated skillCommands list sourced from skill.list (app.skills), separate from the / slash commands. Selecting inserts /skill text which submits via the existing command path.
Fixed - V2 machine has a dedicated skill-inline popover routed to a separate skills accessor (skill-only suggestions), so $ never filters or inserts ordinary commands.
Fixed - replaceSkillTrigger replaces the $ token using persisted.cursor and appends the trailing suffix, with a non-destructive fallback. Covered by a mid-line cursor test.
